captionBefore: Left: 15 simulated populations from the same start (thin) and the mean over 300 runs (black) against the deterministic curve $N_0e^{rt}$ (green, dashed) — the sample mean is compared with the theoretical exponential, although finite-run error can be large and most single paths look nothing like it. Right: the fraction observed to hit 0 before a cap against founder number $N_0$ (dots with 95 % intervals for this capped Bernoulli outcome), compared with the eventual-extinction formula (green). The caps are 150 individuals or 30,000 jump steps. Hold $r$ fixed and raise the turnover $d$ to see extinction risk grow; set $r\le0$ and extinction is certain.
captionAfter: Left: 15 simulated populations from the same start (thin) and the mean over 300 runs (black) against the deterministic curve $N_0e^{rt}$ (green, dashed) — the sample mean is compared with the theoretical exponential, although finite-run error can be large and most single paths look nothing like it. Right: the fraction observed to hit 0 before a cap against founder number $N_0$ (dots with 95 % intervals for this capped Bernoulli outcome), compared with the eventual-extinction formula (green). The caps are 150 individuals or 30,000 jump steps. Hold $r$ fixed and raise the turnover $d$ to see extinction risk grow; set $r\le0$ and extinction is certain. Process and ruin interpretations require strictly positive $b=d+r$ and $d$. The readout flags invalid control combinations; their drawn curves are outside this birth–death model and are not process evidence.
